name: Geologist
title: Geologist & Geoscientist
intro: From Class 12 Science to a geoscientist: B.Sc Geology, M.Sc Geology or Applied Geology, the UPSC Combined Geo-Scientist Examination, then GSI, CGWB, mining, petroleum, consulting or research.

phases.title: Class 12 Science
phases.summary: PCM or PCB; PCM is the most common background.
points: Class 12 Science leads to B.Sc Geology.
PCM is the most common background.
Geology suits students who like the outdoors, maps and natural science — field trips are long.

phases.title: B.Sc Geology
phases.summary: Or a science degree with geology.
points: Study B.Sc Geology, or a science degree with geology as a subject.
A B.Sc alone is not enough for UPSC geologist posts.
Field work, lab analysis and GIS/remote sensing are all part of the job — start early.

phases.title: M.Sc Geology / Applied Geology
points: UPSC geologist posts need a master's in Geology, Applied Geology or another earth-science subject listed in the notice.
Private-sector roles usually ask for an M.Sc or M.Tech in geology or applied geology.
Research routes in universities, IITs and national institutes often go via NET/PhD.

phases.title: UPSC Combined Geo-Scientist Examination
points: Stage III: personality test. The exam fills Geologist, Geophysicist, Chemist and Hydrogeologist posts; age limits are in the current notice.

phases.title: Join GSI / CGWB or industry
phases.summary: Government geoscience bodies, or mining, petroleum, consulting and research.
points: Government entry: Group A central services start at Level 10 of the 7th CPC pay matrix (₹56,100 entry basic), plus DA, HRA and other allowances.
Government employers: Geological Survey of India, Central Ground Water Board, state mining and groundwater departments; senior officers reach director-level posts.
Private: mining companies, oil & gas, geotechnical consultancies and environmental firms, where field allowances add up.
